description: Agent Customs Records: submit duty drawback claim records with the duty payments and proof they answer to: each claim with its id, reference, the import entry it draws on, the duty it claims back, the currency, the moment filed, whether it rests on export or destruction and the proof it asserts; each duty payment with its id, the import entry, the moment paid and the amount; each export or destruction proof on file with its id, reference, kind and the moment the goods were exported or destroyed. The signed report gives the claims and the entries, each claim against the duty payment on its entry, each claimed amount against the duty recorded as paid, each entry against the claims that name it, and each asserted proof against the records on file, and counts them, and names divergent drawback claim records: a claim filed on an entry whose duty payment is not in the records, a claimed amount that exceeds the duty recorded as paid, the same entry claimed twice, and export or destruction proof asserted in a claim with no record of it on file; then proof of another kind than the claim rests on and proof dated after the claim, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No claims, or a claim asserting no proof, leaves those points unverified. Claims, entries, payments and proofs match by letters and digits, the duty payments on one entry add together and a claimed amount compares with them to the cent, and dates compare by the day. This reads the claims made to get duty back: wever_customs-duty-check reads duty as paid at entry against the entry’s classified value and rate, while the drawback check reads each claim to recover that duty against the duty recorded as paid and the export or destruction proof on file. Verdict customs_drawback_divergent, customs_drawback_partial, customs_drawback_unverified or customs_drawback_consistent. POST /api/customs-drawback-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
